comments.author: SptAkiModsEnjoyer
comments.body_html:
Hello and thanx for the mod.

I’m having an issue with helmet insurance prices. At 25x, they don’t go above 30k, while the cowboy hat is priced at 82–102k.

Rigs and vests are also too cheap to insure until plates are added. Some rigs and plates don’t allow plate changes, which makes them too cheap to insure. I think this may be related to why helmets aren’t getting higher insurance costs — they don’t swap armor the way other gear does.

I’d love to see this fixed, or at least have the option to use much higher pricing multipliers, like 250x, to better balance helmet insurance.

Thanx again for your hard work.

comments.author: Xenyx
comments.body_html:
Hi - this is something I’d noticed too.

It seems some gear has very low price values defined in SPT\SPT_Data\database\templates\handbook.json, which is where SPT’s insurance price function gets the item’s price from.

For example: the MTEK Flux helmet is valued at only 1429 rubles, and after insurance price calculation with Prapor, it costs ~272 rubles to insure. This is definitely not right, as it’s a relatively high-end helmet which Ragman LL4 sells for >100k.

So the core of the problem is handbook.json having bad price values for some items. With the way this mod currently functions (simply multiplying the final price provided by GetRoublePriceToInsureItemWithTrader), fixing the base prices in handbook.json is not really within the scope of what this mod does (though I might look into that).

I will think over some ways I could possibly circumvent this (like pulling trader or flea price for some items instead). Or as you suggested: raising the multiplier ceiling. Though it’s worth mentioning a major caveat to running a very high multiplier to fix poorly priced items would be correctly priced ones in the same category costing ridiculous amounts to insure. E.g. Tagilla’s welding mask going from ~25k to 6.25 million with a 250x multiplier.
